/// What code asks of the lane it runs in, whichever kind that is.
export abstract class Lanes {
    /// True once the job or worker this code runs in was asked to stop, so a
    /// long loop either may run can end early. A job that returns then still
    /// settles stopped; a worker settles with what it returns. On the web a
    /// job from a release bake without wasmFuel has no fuel and cannot be
    /// interrupted, so one that never polls runs to its end, and without
    /// threads it holds the page until it returns. False on the main lane and
    /// in an audio processor.
    static stopping(): bool;
}

/// A started job, worker or audio processor.
export abstract class Lane {
    /// The host's handle on the lane; 0 once released.
    handle: u32;

    /// Where the lane is in its life; never waits.
    get state(): LaneState;

    /// True until the lane is done, fails or stops.
    get running(): bool;

    /// Why the lane failed: a throw, a trap or a processor's overrun block.
    /// Null unless it failed.
    get failed(): string?;

    /// Ends the lane early; it then settles stopped, unless it was already
    /// over or is a worker that returns or throws first. A job that has not
    /// started never runs; a running one is interrupted. A worker's awaits
    /// settle with kWaitStopping and Lanes.stopping turns true; one that
    /// awaits again ends there, and one still running past a short grace is
    /// interrupted. On the web only a lane with fuel, which debug bakes and
    /// wasmFuel bakes give every lane, can be interrupted: a job without fuel
    /// stops only once it sees Lanes.stopping turn true, and a worker without
    /// it only at an await. A processor leaves the mix at a block boundary.
    stop(): void;

    /// Releases the handle now instead of when it is collected; a lane still
    /// running is stopped.
    release(): void;
}

/// A job or worker, whose result crosses back as a deep copy once it
/// returns.
export abstract class ResultLane<R> extends Lane {
    /// The outcome without waiting; null until the lane is over. The result
    /// is decoded once, so each call after answers the same Settled, kept
    /// until release.
    peek(): Settled<R>?;

    /// As peek for a result decoded into out without allocating: true once
    /// out holds it; false, leaving out alone, while the lane runs and once
    /// it failed or was stopped, which state tells apart. R is a class of
    /// numbers, a StaticArray of numbers or a typed array, its arrays as
    /// long as the ones returned.
    @decodesInPlace
    peekInto(out: R): bool;

    /// Releases the handle as Lane.release does, and the decoded outcome
    /// with it.
    override release(): void;

    /// Settles on an advance after the lane is over, never inside the call
    /// that asked: fulfills with its result, rejects with why it failed, and
    /// is cancelled when the lane was stopped, with the reason peek gives.
    /// Cancelling it stops the lane. Each call answers the same promise.
    /// ```as
    /// async function load(bytes: Uint8Array): Promise<Tile> {
    ///     return await Jobs.run(decodeTile, bytes).promise();
    /// }
    /// ```
    promise(): Promise<R>;
}
